newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-H.Smith sees housing pick-up mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-H.Smith sees housing pick-up mid-1997.

text.p: Shipping, engineering and hardware group Howard Smith Ltd said on Tuesday it expected a pick-up in its hardware sales in the first half of 1997/98 as lower interest rates flowed through to increased housing starts.
"Now is the time you can put more credence on (better) forecasts," Howard Smith's managing director Ken Moss told a media briefing.

"Our forecast would be that we may do a little better in the remaining months of this financial year - and going into the next financial year, I think that pick-up will be stronger but the degree of that strength remains to be seen," he said.
Moss said the lag between lower interest rates and increased housing starts was probably between three and six months.
The Reserve Bank of Australia cut official interest rates three times between July and December 1996, taking the cash rate to 6.0 percent.
Howard Smith earlier posted a 15.7 percent rise in pre-abnormal net profit to A$46.95 million for the six months to December 31, 1996.
The company said its BBC Hardware chain recorded a 3.5 percent increase in sales on the previous corresponding half.

This was driven by a 12 percent rise in sales on the retail side due to the expansion of its Hardwarehouse chain of stores. "There is no question the market is improving, albeit extremely slowly," said Howard Smith's deputy managing director and hardware division head, Ian Tsicalas.
"We had a strong January - a lot of builders came back a bit earlier than they usually do," Tsicalas said.
Tsicalas said a wetter than usual February in New South Wales meant there was backlog of orders that had not been converted to sales for delivery reasons which Howard Smith expected to be satisfied.
Tsicalas said the Hardware group had gained market share in terms of cash sales and trade sales had at least held its share in the first half.

"With another dozen Hardware House shares to be fully under construction by June, plus quite a few more to follow that, they will obviously grab a lot of market share particularly in the cash side of the market," Tsicalas said.
Tsicalas said he expected this extra market share to be wrenched from all of its existing competitors as well as from a growth in the market which was being nurtured by the company's own expansion.
"Our numbers on our existing Hardware House stores tell us that we have grown the market to a fair extent as well," he said.
Tsicalas said the hardware division was also looking at a number of expansion opportunities for its Hardwarehouse chain in Southeast Asia.
"It's not a high priority but it is a priority we will certainly pursue," he said.
Howard Smith expected to spend about A$80 million in capital expenditure for the 1996/97 financial year after spending A$24.5 million in the first half.
However, the total amount would depend on the timing of the planned construction of further Hardwarehouse stores.
Howard Smith shares closed 15 cents higher at A$11.15.
- Michael Stapleton, Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
